{{see also|Rado's theorem (Ramsey theory)}}

In [[mathematics]], '''Radó's theorem''' is a result about [[harmonic function]]s, named after [[Tibor Radó]]. Informally, it says that any "nice looking" shape without holes can be smoothly deformed into a disk.

Suppose Ω is an [[open set|open]], [[Connected space|connected]] and [[convex set|convex]] [[subset]] of the [[Euclidean space]] '''R'''<sup>2</sup> with [[smooth function|smooth]] [[Boundary (topology)|boundary]] ∂Ω and suppose that '''D''' is the [[unit disk]]. Then, given any [[homeomorphism]]
μ : ∂'''D''' → ∂Ω, there exists a unique harmonic function ''u'' : '''D''' → Ω such that ''u'' = μ on ∂'''D''' and ''u'' is a [[diffeomorphism]].
